name: Pulse — the Living City map
firstPrinciple: The map is not a wayfinding surface, it is a live broadcast of the city's social energy. Every pixel exists to answer one felt question — "is tonight happening, and where is it happening?" — in under five seconds, with zero tutorial. Three physical metaphors carry everything: HEAT (where energy is), CONSTELLATIONS (where crews are), and TIDE (where the night is going). People are never rendered as individuals; the atomic social object on the map is the crew, and the heat is generated BY your social graph — which is the one thing crowd-utility apps (Current, NOITE) structurally cannot copy and Snap Map's individual-first model doesn't do.
coreLoop: GLANCE (open at any hour; the city is visibly breathing — heat tempo, crew constellations, story rings, tide forecast) → READ (hottest district, which venues have crews and fresh reels, when tonight peaks) → TAP (venue opens: activity level, merged place-reel, groups in the pool, event, cost) → ACT (long-press to Rally your crew there, or tap a constellation to send a pool invite) → CONVERGE (OMW comets with live ETAs animate your crew arriving; the venue mark charges up) → FEED BACK (your attendance warms the heat, extends your crew streak, deepens your venue relationship, and your posted clip brightens the story ring) → tomorrow's glance is richer because of last night. The loop closes on a night out, not on time-in-app.
mapStructure: Three altitudes with semantic zoom — marks morph, they don't just scale. A0 ORBIT (globe): city nodes sized by live out-count; only Velmont is live; tapping it triggers a cinematic dive (exists today). A1 CITY (default): districts render as breathing organisms — heat blobs whose pulse TEMPO encodes fill-rate (Arches beats fast, Docks barely breathes), district name + one-word state ('On fire'), crew constellations as small star-clusters, event beacons as vertical light columns, and the Night Tide bar along the bottom. A2 STREET (zoom 2–3): individual venue marks with three concentric readable states — inner heat core (busyness), story ring (content freshness, visibly cooling over ~2h), and a crew-count badge. Movement: tap city from orbit; pinch/step-zoom between A1 and A2; tapping any district glow at A1 flies to A2 centered on it; tapping a venue at any altitude opens the venue sheet. One surface, no separate tabs — stories, events, and the pool are all reached THROUGH the map.

keyFeatures.how: Aggregate heat from check-ins, RSVPs, and story volume, weighted toward your extended graph — venues where friends-of-friends are out glow warmer FOR YOU. Rendered as blobs that literally beat: animation tempo = fill rate, and heat visibly cools within ~2 hours of the signal so freshness is legible without timestamps. A city-level 'Velmont: 128 BPM' pulse pill summarizes the whole night in one number.
keyFeatures.ceoQuestions: Discovery: answers 'where is good RIGHT NOW' in one glance. Intuitive: heat=busy is the universal grammar Snap proved; tempo and cooling add information without adding UI. Repeat engagement: the map is never the same twice. Identity vs imitation: our heat is generated by the social layer, so utility compounds with the network — Current/NOITE can't copy it, and Snap doesn't personalize it. Expansion: promoted glow is the venue-revenue lever.

keyFeatures.feature: Crew Constellations (the group is the map object)
keyFeatures.how: A crew out together fuses into one constellation mark — member stars orbiting slowly, connected by faint lines — anchored to their venue. Strangers see only aggregate counts ('3 crews here'); a constellation becomes named/avatared only when that crew lights its Beacon: an explicit, per-night, time-boxed broadcast (auto-off 4am) to mutuals and the Pool. Tapping a beaconed constellation opens the crew card with a one-tap pool invite. Your own crew is always visible to you.
keyFeatures.ceoQuestions: Discovery: shows which venues have joinable crews, not just crowds. Friction: tap-constellation→pool-invite collapses see/decide/ask into one gesture. Intuitive: person-shaped marks (Zenly's Gathering Pin, evolved to group-first). Repeat: 'your friends are together at Archive 9' is the core FOMO trigger. Identity: nobody else renders GROUPS as the first-class map primitive — this is Func's signature mark.

keyFeatures.how: Long-press any venue → 'Rally the crew here' pings your group with venue, event, and cost context attached. As members accept, they appear (group-visible only) as comet trails converging on the venue with live ETAs, and the venue mark visibly charges up as the crew assembles. The pre-arrival phase — 'who's actually coming, how far out are they' — becomes a watchable, tappable animation.
keyFeatures.ceoQuestions: Friction: kills the plan-in-chat/execute-on-map split; the map is where nights are STARTED, not just observed. Repeat: the converge phase drives 5–10 opens per night, all high-intent. Intuitive: long-press-to-summon is one gesture with an obvious result. Identity: it literally animates our success metric — invite→accept→attended as a closed loop on screen.

keyFeatures.feature: Place Reels (stories that exist only on the map)
keyFeatures.how: Clips are postable only at recognized venues and viewable only by tapping the venue — no stories tab, ever. Fresh content renders as a bright ring that cools over ~2 hours (nightlife's real relevance horizon, not 24h). Tapping plays a merged reel of the PLACE (everyone's clips, not one author's feed) with a persistent 'Go' action: directions, event page, or pool. Posting is framed to the poster as 'put this place on the map.'
keyFeatures.ceoQuestions: Discovery: answers the go/no-go questions — vibe, crowd, music, line. Intuitive: tap-the-glow-to-see-inside is Snap-proven. Repeat: content supply makes the glance rewarding even when no friend is out. Identity: map-first content inverts Instagram's failed bolt-on; every story view reinforces the discovery loop. Expansion: venue-posted reels backfill cold-start neighborhoods and become the promoted-content revenue surface.

keyFeatures.feature: Night Tide (time scrubber: forecast, live, afterglow)
keyFeatures.how: A tide bar along the bottom scrubs tonight from 8pm to 3am: behind now = actual heat, at now = live, ahead of now = forecast rendered as ghosted heat (from RSVPs, events, and historical patterns) — so at 6pm Tuesday the map shows Friday building. Sunday delivers Afterglow: your crew's route replayed as footprints, feeding crew streaks ('4 weekends running') and your crew's home-bar flame.
keyFeatures.ceoQuestions: Repeat engagement: this is what makes the map worth opening on a Tuesday — the peak night is the event, the tide is the ambient layer for the other five days. Discovery: 'peaks at 11' is decide-before-you-leave utility. Expansion: forecast quality is a compounding data moat per city. Identity: we model the ARC of a night, which a busyness-utility app has no reason to do.

keyFeatures.how: Privacy is part of the visual grammar, not a settings page: no individual live dot exists anywhere in the system, crews appear only via the explicit per-night Beacon with a visible countdown, and a single time-boxed Ghost toggle (tonight / 24h / until I turn it off) suppresses even aggregate contribution. What others can see is always inspectable in one tap.
keyFeatures.ceoQuestions: Intuitive: legible privacy IS usability (Snap's Ghost Mode lesson); users who trust the map use the map. Friction: one toggle, no maze. Identity: women-first safety and the inversion of Tinder Social's fatal mistake are core brand — 'this venue is popping' is discovery, 'this person is here' is a headline we architecturally cannot generate.

firstTimeUserStory: 0–10s: App opens on the orbit view — a dark globe with glowing city nodes and a live counter ('2,341,882 people out on Earth'). One node is ringed: Velmont. She taps it. 10–20s: Cinematic dive into a neon city that is visibly ALIVE — the Arches district beats fast and hot cyan, Old Quarter shimmers pink, the Docks barely breathe; a pill reads 'Velmont: 128 BPM · 1,847 out'. No labels needed: hot = busy is instantly decoded. 20–35s: She taps the hottest glow. Archive 9's card slides up: 'On fire · 6 groups in the pool · ~£34 all-in', and the bright ring around it auto-plays a 10-second merged reel of the room right now. She now knows more about tonight than any review app could tell her. 35–50s: A small constellation of avatars orbits the venue — 'Rooftop Gremlins · 4 going · looking for another crew'. She taps it and sees the pool invite button; the map just showed her people, not just places. 50–60s: A tooltip appears exactly once: 'Long-press anywhere to rally your crew.' She long-presses her corner of the city, sees the Rally sheet, and understands the entire product — see the night, find the people, start the plan — without a single tutorial screen. Beating the Snap Map bar: three-layer grammar (heat / crew marks / tap-through content), one gesture each, five-second decode.
differentiators: Graph-generated heat: the busyness layer is produced by your extended social graph, so utility compounds with network density — structurally uncopyable by crowd-data utilities and un-prioritizable inside Snap's individual-first, buried map.
The crew as the atomic map object: constellations, Beacons, Rally, and streaks are all group-first primitives; every competitor renders individuals or venues, never groups.
Map-only ephemeral content with a 2-hour cooling horizon tuned to nightlife, versus 24h windows and bolt-on story tabs that go stale.
The map closes loops instead of displaying data: long-press→Rally→OMW comets→attendance means discovery, coordination, and the Pool all execute on one surface.
Privacy as visual grammar: aggregate-only heat with no individual dot in the architecture — the trust posture is a product feature, not a settings compromise.
Night Tide forecast + afterglow gives the map a reason to exist seven days a week, where nightlife utilities are only useful at the Friday-9pm decision moment.
risks: Cold start / ghost-town map: ephemeral content plus sparse users renders a visibly dead city — must launch neighborhood-by-neighborhood with non-UGC backfill (events, venue reels, historical busyness) and never show a region below minimum liveness.
Beacon adoption: if too few crews opt in, the social layer is invisible and Pulse degrades to another heat utility; the Beacon must be woven into the Rally/Pool flow, not offered as a bare toggle.

Perceived-privacy risk despite aggregate-only architecture: 'nightlife app shows where people are' is one bad headline away from Instagram-Map-style backlash; framing and the visible countdown must ship day one.

Animation vs legibility: breathing heat, orbiting constellations, and comets can tip from alive into noisy; needs a strict motion budget (tempo encodes data or it doesn't move) and battery discipline (Zenly's sleep-unless-watched engine).
Graph-weighted heat needs graph density to feel different from generic heat — in city one it may read identically to Current until the network fills in.
Forecast credibility: a wrong 'peaks at 11' burns trust faster than no forecast; ship it as ghosted/uncertain rendering and only where historical data supports it.
prototypeScope: All buildable on the existing Expo/RN SVG stack (VelmontMap.tsx already has the pulse-loop pattern, layered radial-gradient heat, and pan/zoom/hit-test plumbing in app/(tabs)/index.tsx): (1) Breathing heat — per-district staggered Animated loops driving heat-point radius/opacity, tempo mapped to district level (Arches fast, Docks slow); extend HeatPoint with a district/tempo field. (2) City BPM pill — upgrade the existing liveliness pill with an animated beat dot. (3) Crew constellations — 3–4 scripted constellation marks built from existing groups/users data: avatar circles + connecting SVG lines + slow orbit transform, aggregate-count badges on the rest; tap (via the existing hit-test overlay) opens a crew mini-card deep-linking to the Pool tab. (4) Rally demo — long-press detection in the PanResponder → Rally sheet → scripted OMW comets animating along the existing street Path data with counting-down ETA chips, venue halo intensifying as each arrives. (5) Story rings — animated ring on 3 venues; tap plays a fake place-reel modal (3 static images, cooling timestamp, 'Go' button wired to the event screen). (6) Night Tide — a slider crossfading three keyframed heatPoint datasets (9pm/11pm/1am), forward positions rendered dashed/ghosted as forecast. (7) Ghost toggle — cosmetic switch on the Profile tab with the time-box options. Out of scope for the prototype: real location/geofencing, live data, actual video, continuous pinch-zoom (keep the 3-step ZOOMS array), push notifications, and the home-screen widget — all narrated in the pitch instead.

name: The Call — Func Map v3, "The Decision Engine"
firstPrinciple: A night out is a group decision made under time pressure, so the map must be a ranked instrument, not a mirror. Snap Map shows you the city and leaves the deciding to you; Func's map computes the decision. Every pixel is either evidence (heat, cost, your graph, freshness) or an action (Call it, vote, OMW, join a group) — anything that is neither gets deleted. The measure of the surface is one number: seconds from open to a locked group plan, target under 10 for evidence and under 60 including the group's votes.
coreLoop: Open at 9pm → the map is already framed for YOU TONIGHT: your active crew chip and budget are applied, and 2–3 venues carry oversized 'Match Beacons' (glow scaled by fit = live heat × budget fit × extended-graph presence × distance), with a Top-3 rail naming them. Tap a beacon → Decision Card: four evidence rows (busyness + trend arrow, £ all-in meter vs your budget, 'who' in aggregate terms, a 2-hour-fresh place reel) and ONE primary CTA: 'Call it.' → Call it broadcasts a two-button verdict (In / Nah) to the crew directly on their maps; majority — or a 10-minute timer — locks the plan → the venue pin becomes the Plan Pin and the map enters Night Mode: Convoy layer shows crew ETAs converging (opt-in, plan-scoped, auto-expiring location) → attend → post-night one-taps (story to the map, 'what did tonight cost?', vouch your co-attendees) feed heat, cost ranges, and the trust graph → next weekend the ranking is smarter and the loop is faster. Between weekends the same surface runs the ambient loop: footprints of last weekend's route, crew streaks, venue loyalty ranks, and the city's live pulse — the Tuesday glance that Zenly proved is where retention lives.
mapStructure: Three altitudes, one continuous camera, each answering exactly one question. ALTITUDE 1 — GLOBE ('is the world out?'): the existing stylised night-globe; city nodes sized by live count, arcs, global counter; Velmont pulses as the only live node, others read 'landing soon'. Tap a node to dive. ALTITUDE 2 — CITY ('where should we go?'): the SVG Velmont map with the full decision grammar — aggregate heat wash (k≥10, breathes on ~60s frames), venue Match Beacons ranked for the active crew lens, Gathering Pins where crews have fused at a venue, Pool Beacons (other groups' open invites), the Top-3 rail, and the crew/budget/time chip row pinned on top. Pan + zoom (buttons now, pinch later). ALTITUDE 3 — VENUE FOCUS ('do we commit?'): tapping a venue pushes the camera in, dims surrounding streets, and slides the Decision Card up as a bottom sheet over the still-visible block — you never leave the map; stories, cost, and Call It all live inside this sheet. Movement: tap descends, back-swipe or pinch-out ascends; locking a plan re-frames the city altitude around the Plan Pin (Night Mode). Stories have no tab — the only route to any content is down through these altitudes, so every view reinforces the discovery loop.

keyFeatures.how: A pinned chip row — [crew ▾] [tonight/when ▾] [£ budget] — re-ranks the whole city. Venue glow size = fit score (heat × budget fit × graph presence × distance); the Top-3 rail names the winners with one-line reasons ('busy, £20–30, 2 groups you know'). With zero friends the lens degrades gracefully to heat × budget × distance — single-player utility on day one.
keyFeatures.ceoQuestions: Easier discovery: the map answers 'where' in one glance instead of making you scan pins. Less friction: no filter screens — three chips, live re-rank. First-time intuitive: glow = go is the Snap Map grammar everyone already reads; the rail is a fallback for map-illiterate users. Repeat engagement: ranking improves with every attended night. Future expansion: fit score is where venue-paid promotion slots in transparently ('Promoted' beacons), and it scales to any city. Identity: ranking BY GROUP is something individual-first Snap structurally can't do — this is Func's spine, not imitation.

keyFeatures.how: One bottom sheet, four fixed evidence rows, in decision order: (1) busyness — level + trend arrow ('filling up'); (2) cost meter — £min–max all-in from the existing costBreakdown model, rendered against your budget chip; (3) who — aggregate only ('3 crews from your wider graph in', avatars only with explicit opt-in); (4) freshness — a place reel of ≤2h-old stories with visible decay. One primary CTA: Call It. Secondary: directions, event page, save.
keyFeatures.ceoQuestions: Easier discovery: the go/no-go questions (busy? how much? who? vibe?) answered in one card — the exact info the nightlife-utility competitors scatter across screens. Less friction: evidence to action is one tap. First-time intuitive: it's a card, the universal mobile pattern. Repeat engagement: cost ranges sharpen from crowd receipts, so the card gets more trustworthy. Future expansion: ticketing, line-skip, and table booking are just more rows/CTAs on this card. Identity: £-on-the-map is Func's original signal — no benchmark app shows money, and cost is the real decision input for 18–26.

keyFeatures.feature: Call It → Group Verdict (one-tap plan, on-map voting)
keyFeatures.how: Call It drops a proposed Plan Pin on every crew member's map with a two-button verdict: In / Nah. Majority locks it; a visible 10-minute timer auto-locks to prevent stalls; the caller can override-lock ('captain's call'). Locked plan converts the venue pin into the crew's Plan Pin and posts one line to the crew chat. Long-press any venue does the same — map-driven plan creation, no chat archaeology.
keyFeatures.ceoQuestions: Easier discovery→action: collapses the plan-in-chat/execute-on-map split the research flags. Less friction: the whole group decision is three taps total across the crew. First-time intuitive: two buttons. Repeat engagement: being summoned to vote is a high-signal, low-spam notification that reopens the map. Future expansion: the verdict object generalises to Pool accept/decline and paid events (vote-then-split). Identity: group consensus as a first-class map interaction exists nowhere else — it is the mechanic that makes Func group-first rather than claiming it.

keyFeatures.how: Once a plan locks, members can flip on Convoy: live dots + ETAs converging on the Plan Pin. Scope is the mechanism and the privacy story: visible only to this crew, only for this plan, auto-expires at night's end; one Ghost toggle (3h/tonight/indefinite) kills it instantly. When members co-locate at the venue, dots fuse into one animated Gathering Pin — 'your crew is together at Archive 9' — the map's most tappable object and Func's core FOMO trigger.
keyFeatures.ceoQuestions: Less friction: kills the 'where are you / 5 min away' text volley — the pre-arrival phase is most of a night's coordination pain (the proven OMW mechanic). First-time intuitive: dots moving toward a pin needs no explanation. Repeat engagement: watching the crew converge is the single most compulsive glance-loop in the category (Zenly's lesson). Future expansion: Convoy ETA is the substrate for meet-the-other-group logistics in Pool and for venue arrival predictions venues will pay for. Identity: time-boxed, plan-scoped location is the anti-Snap position — Func never tracks you, it escorts a plan — which honours the aggregate-only thesis while still delivering live presence.

keyFeatures.feature: Pulse stories — heat that cools, viewable only through the map
keyFeatures.how: Posting from a recognised venue at night 'puts the place on the map': the venue visibly brightens, and its Decision Card reel gains the clip. Stories decay hard on a 2-hour freshness horizon (nightlife's real relevance window, vs Instagram's stale 24h) and the venue visually cools as they age. No stories tab exists; the reel is reachable only via venue focus, and every reel ends on a Go/Call It frame. Cold-start backfill: venue-posted clips, event data, and historical busyness keep the map from ever reading dead.
keyFeatures.ceoQuestions: Easier discovery: content answers 'is it actually good RIGHT NOW', the one thing reviews and venue marketing can't. First-time intuitive: heat + tap-for-stories is exactly the 40-billion-opens Snap Map behaviour. Repeat engagement: posting is framed as status ('you lit this venue up') and feeds Place Loyalty ranks later. Future expansion: promoted reels and venue story tools are the Snap-validated monetisation path. Identity: story-as-decaying-liveness-signal (not media gallery) is a genuine inversion of every benchmark — content exists to produce a meetup, per the inspiration artifact's best idea, minus its separate-surface mistake.

keyFeatures.feature: Pool Beacons + the Tuesday ambient layer
keyFeatures.how: Other groups' open invites render as distinct ringed beacons on the city map ('4 of us, Skyline Rooftop, 10pm — join us'), gated by the trust system (vouch or 2 mutuals to knock), so the hero Pool mechanic is discovered spatially, not in a list. Off-peak, the same map runs ambient: last weekend's footprint route, crew streaks ('4 weekends running'), venue loyalty ranks, and a home-screen widget of crew state + city pulse.
keyFeatures.ceoQuestions: Easier discovery: groups-to-meet become a thing you SEE near where you already are. Less friction: knock → their crew gets a verdict vote — same two-button grammar as Call It. First-time intuitive: a beacon with faces and a note reads instantly; the trust gate is one legible line. Repeat engagement: the ambient layer is the answer to 'worth opening on a Tuesday' — streaks, footprints, and the widget fill the five off-nights. Future expansion: loyalty ranks and streaks are the retention scaffolding venues later sponsor. Identity: Pool-on-map is the one intersection nobody holds (heat utilities have no graph, friend maps have no venues, Snap has no groups) — it is Func's moat drawn directly onto the centrepiece surface.

firstTimeUserStory: 0–5s: App opens straight onto Velmont at city altitude — no splash quiz, no tutorial. Dark city, three glowing beacons breathing, sea at the bottom, a ticking '214 out tonight' counter. One coach line, shown once, over the map: 'Glow = busy. £ = the damage. Tap one.' The Snap Map grammar does the rest — nothing to learn. 5–20s: Their eye goes to the biggest beacon (Archive 9, hottest by design). The Top-3 rail at the bottom confirms it in words: '1. Archive 9 — rammed, £25–40 · 2. Skyline — filling up, £22–35 · 3. The Keg — cheap & busy, £10–18.' They tap Archive 9. 20–40s: Camera pushes in, streets dim, the Decision Card slides up: busyness arrow climbing, cost meter, '6 groups in tonight', and a story reel that autoplays a 4-second clip of the room going off — posted 12 minutes ago, timestamp glowing fresh. They understand the entire product: the map knows where's good, what it costs, and shows proof. 40–60s: They hit the big button — 'Call it.' A friendly interrupt: 'Who's coming? Start your crew.' Two contacts picked, invite sent, and the map shows their proposed Plan Pin with two empty vote slots waiting to fill. They arrived alone with zero friends on the app and still got real utility (where's good + cost) in 20 seconds; the product's first ask of them is the product's whole point: bring your people. No screen so far has been anything other than the map.
differentiators: Ranked, not rendered: the only nightlife map that computes 'best for YOUR group tonight' (heat × budget × graph × distance) instead of showing an unranked city and wishing you luck

Money on the map: £ min–max all-in cost as a first-class visual signal and ranking input — no benchmark app (Snap, Zenly, Jagat, Current, NOITE) shows cost at all, and it's the #1 real decision input for 18–26
Group verdict as a map interaction: Call It / In / Nah with a lock timer turns the map into the place plans get DECIDED, collapsing the chat-vs-map split every competitor suffers

Plan-scoped location: Convoy shows live crew ETAs only inside a locked plan and auto-expires — live presence without surveillance, honouring aggregate-only heat (k≥10) while Instagram takes congressional flak for always-on friend maps
Heat generated BY your social layer: crews checked in at venues make the heat, so utility compounds with the network — structurally uncopyable by venue-data utilities like Current/NOITE
Stories with no tab: place reels decay on a 2-hour nightlife horizon and are reachable only through the map, so every content view is a discovery act and every post 'puts the place on the map'

Pool Beacons: groups-meet-groups (the hero mechanic and the trust architecture) discovered spatially on the centrepiece surface — the intersection (venue layer + group graph + map-first) that no incumbent holds
risks: Cold-start density is existential: sparse ephemeral content leaves a visibly dead map (the nightlife-app graveyard's shared cause). Mitigation is architectural — neighbourhood-gated launch, never render a region below minimum liveness, backfill with venue/event/historical data — but it must be enforced, not aspired to.

Ranking trust: one Friday where the #1 beacon is a dead room and users stop believing the map. Fit scores need conservative confidence handling (show 'filling up' honestly, decay stale signals fast) and the Top-3 rail must state its reasons so wrongness is at least legible.

Verdict stall or resentment: voting can add friction to groups that decide by inertia, and 'captain's call' override can breed friction inside crews. The 10-minute auto-lock and default-in semantics need real-user testing before the mechanic is trusted with the hero position.

Convoy privacy misread: any individual live dot, however scoped, risks being reported as 'Func tracks you'. The time-box, plan-scope, and one-toggle Ghost must be visually undeniable in the UI itself, and women-first safety review must gate the feature per the thesis.
'Who's there' vs k-anonymity tension: '2 groups you know are in' can deanonymise in small graphs. The aggregate threshold must apply to graph-presence copy, not just heat pixels.

Promoted beacons can poison the instrument: the moment paid placement outranks truth, the sub-10-second promise dies. Promotion must be capped, labelled, and never allowed into the #1 slot on falsified evidence.
Prototype perf: beacons + convoy dots + heat pulse + ticker exceed the 'three animations max' budget from the v2 review on old Androids; the demo needs an animation-tier fallback.
Scope gravity: Call It, Convoy, Pool Beacons, and stories each tempt a full build; the pitch demo needs the staged, scripted versions only — the v2 lesson (fake the right things) applies double here.
prototypeScope: Fully buildable on the existing Expo/RN-SVG stack with no new dependencies, extending VelmontMap.tsx, store.tsx, and the existing Venue/CostItem/PoolInvite/WorldCity models. IN SCOPE: (1) Group Lens chip row — crew selector + £ budget chips; fit score computed client-side from existing venue.level, avgSpend, groupsTonight, and district distance; beacon glow radius/opacity scale with score; Top-3 rail with generated reason strings. (2) Decision Card bottom sheet — busyness row with a faked trend arrow, cost meter rendered from existing costBreakdown min/max against the budget chip, aggregate 'who' line from groups data, and a story row of 2–4 hand-authored 'posted Xm ago' stills with decay tinting (no video; timed stills sell the reel). (3) Call It → Verdict — staged demo theatre: crew votes arrive on setTimeout (In… In…), lock animation converts the venue pin to a Plan Pin; entirely in-memory via store.tsx, resets on relaunch per the pristine-demo rule. (4) Convoy — 3 dots animated along existing street path strokes toward the Plan Pin with fake decreasing ETAs; fuse into a pulsing Gathering Pin on arrival; Ghost toggle flips the layer off. (5) Pool Beacons — ringed pins rendered from existing poolInvites with a 'Vouch or 2 mutuals' gate line, knock → same verdict UI. (6) A demo-only time scrubber (21:00→01:00) that re-weights heatPoints and story freshness so the presenter can show the map cooling and warming — the cheapest possible proof that heat is alive. (7) Globe altitude unchanged from v2. OUT OF SCOPE (stated in pitch as backend-era work): real ranking/telemetry, video reels, push-driven votes, real location/ETAs, k-anonymity pipeline, widget, streak persistence. Respect the three-concurrent-animations budget: beacon pulse, convoy dots, and ticker — pause the ticker while Convoy runs.

name: The Floor — Func's living night map
firstPrinciple: Every pixel of light on the map is authored by a real group doing something tonight. The map is not a chart of the city — it is a stage the city performs on. Heat is never synthetic: venue glow is generated by your extended social graph's check-ins and stories, so watching the map is watching people, and the only way to be seen on it is to actually go out. Corollary rules that everything else derives from: (1) groups are the atomic visible unit — no individual ever renders alone without explicit opt-in; (2) content lives ONLY on the map — there is no stories tab, so every view reinforces place-discovery; (3) light decays fast (~2h ember cooling) so brightness always means NOW.
coreLoop: WATCH → WANT → RALLY → PLANT → PERFORM → (feed the next watcher). You open the map at 9pm to glance at the city: three venues burning with story rings, your friends' crew flag flying at one of them. Watching creates the want ("they're together at Archive 9 right now" — the Zenly Gathering Pin FOMO, group-scale). One long-press Rallies your crew to a venue; ETA arcs animate as people go OMW. On arrival your crew's flag plants — which itself heats the venue for everyone else. You post a clip to the venue's ring, framed as "put this place on the map." Your performance is the next person's watch. Off-peak, the Afterglow layer (footprints, crew streaks, home-bar loyalty, upcoming marquees) keeps the Tuesday glance rewarding, closing the daily-habit loop without notifications.
mapStructure: Three altitudes, one continuous camera — never a page navigation. (1) GLOBE (exists in prototype): the planet at night; cities render as single glow-points whose brightness = live story volume; your home city is pinned. Pinch in. (2) THE FLOOR (city altitude, the default open state): illustrated Velmont with district washes; venues render as story-ringed circles (ring = content, temperature = recency-weighted volume); crew flags are the only person-shaped marks — animated avatar-stack flags planted where 2+ opted-in group members are co-located; ETA arcs curve toward venues with inbound Rallies; ambient district heat underlays it all. (3) FRONT ROW (venue altitude): tapping a venue pushes the camera in and raises the Marquee — a bottom-sheet stage card over the still-visible map: aggregated story reel, crowd meter, cover + avg-spend (existing cost model), the crews flying flags there, vouch-crested host if an open event is on, and one-tap Go actions (Rally / OMW / Directions). Back out with a pinch; the map never leaves the screen. Layer toggles (Tonight / Afterglow / Marquee-upcoming) sit as three chips, Snap-Layers style, but Tonight is always default.

keyFeatures.how: Every venue is a circle whose rim is a segmented ring — one segment per fresh story, colored by age: white-hot (<30min) → cyan → pink ember → gone at ~2h. Ring thickness IS the heat map; there is no separate heat layer to learn. Tap plays a merged place-reel of everyone's clips with a persistent 'Rally' button. Posting UI frames it as 'put Archive 9 on the map.'
keyFeatures.ceoQuestions: Discovery: heat and content are one surface — see it's popping and see WHY in one tap. Intuitive: reuses the universally-decoded IG/Snap story-ring grammar on a place instead of a person; zero onboarding. Repeat engagement: 2h decay means the map is never the same twice — the glance loop. Identity vs imitation: Snap anchors rings to people, Func anchors them to venues with fast nightlife-native decay; aggregate-only, so it also carries the privacy stance. Friction: go/no-go answered (crowd, vibe, music) without texting anyone.

keyFeatures.how: When 2+ members of a group are co-located at a venue with presence on, the group fuses into one animated flag: pole planted on the venue, avatar-stack + group name on the banner, gentle wave animation. Individuals never render alone. Tap → group card: who's out, who's OMW with ETA, mutual-group 'wave' or join-request via the existing pool mechanic.
keyFeatures.ceoQuestions: Discovery: 'which of my people are out and where' in one glance — the single strongest pull-out-the-door trigger (Zenly's Gathering Pin, made the default unit). Intuitive: a flag on a building is self-explanatory. Repeat: ambient curiosity about your graph is the proven daily driver. Identity: group-first marks are Func's thesis made visible — structurally different from Snap/Jagat's individual avatars. Privacy = less friction: aggregate-by-design means no stalking headline. Expansion: flags become the surface for crew streaks, territory, venue loyalty.

keyFeatures.how: Long-press any venue → a half-raised flag appears with your group's avatars greyed; as members accept, avatars light and the flag rises; at quorum it snaps upright with a burst. Accepting members flip to OMW: a dashed ETA arc animates from their district toward the venue (aggregate district-origin, not precise location, unless they opt in). Collapses plan-in-chat/execute-on-map into one gesture.
keyFeatures.ceoQuestions: Friction: the pre-arrival phase ('who's actually coming, how far out') is most of a night's coordination pain — Rally makes it one gesture plus glances. Discovery→action: every story reel ends in a Rally button, so watching converts to going. Intuitive: raising a flag = gathering; needs no copy. Repeat: half-raised flags create open loops you come back to check. Identity: map-driven summoning of a GROUP is Func's own mechanic — amo's OMW was individual, Func's is quorum-based. Expansion: Rally graduates naturally into ticketed events, venue offers on rallied crowds.

keyFeatures.how: Tap venue → camera push + bottom sheet: story reel strip, live crowd meter, cover & avg-spend from the existing cost-breakdown model, crews currently flying flags, tonight's event bill, and Go actions. If a stranger-visible open event is on, the host renders with their vouch crest here.
keyFeatures.ceoQuestions: Discovery: answers all go/no-go questions (crowd, cost, who's there, what's on) in one card — beats the nightlife-utility apps' data with social proof they can't have. Friction: directions/RSVP/Rally one tap from content. Intuitive: bottom-sheet-over-map is the maps-app pattern everyone knows. Repeat: cost transparency (Func's existing differentiator) gives a reason to check even sober-planning mode. Identity: the venue is the profile page — Func's world is places+groups, not follower feeds.

keyFeatures.how: Members with earned host standing (scarce, tenure-gated, revocable vouches per the reputation research — single-digit slots, public attribution, voucher-weighted, mutual-pair discounted) get a small crest on their flag ONLY when hosting an open event. Tap: 'Vouched by Maya + 2 you know' with shared-history receipts. Conduct-only semantics; never gates map access.
keyFeatures.ceoQuestions: Discovery: makes stranger-joinable events trustable at the exact decision moment — unlocks the pool/join loop for people with no crew out tonight. Intuitive: a crest on a flag reads as rank instantly. Identity: 'I'll put my name on the list for you' is nightlife-native culture, and no competitor has trust infrastructure on a map. Repeat/expansion: standing accrues from hosting well → people host more → more open events on the map. Safety-as-feature strengthens the 18+ positioning.

keyFeatures.how: Off-peak, the map cools to embers and shows: your crew's footprint from the last night out drawn as a fading route ('your Friday, on the city'), crew streak flame ('4 weekends running'), home-bar loyalty marks ('The Vault — your crew's spot, 5 nights'), and faint marquee glows at venues with upcoming events your graph is eyeing. Plus a home-screen widget of your crew's flag state.
keyFeatures.ceoQuestions: Repeat engagement: this is the answer to 'worth opening on a Tuesday' — memory, status, and anticipation fill the five off-days, per the cross-app retention pattern. Discovery: upcoming-event glow seeds weekend plans early. Identity: crew streaks and group home bars deepen group-first; Snap's Place Loyalty is individual — Func's is 'your crew's spot.' Expansion: loyalty marks are the proven venue-monetization rail (Promoted Places / Place Loyalty playbook). Intuitive: same map, dimmer — no new grammar.

keyFeatures.how: One named switch, time-boxed: Ghost for 3h / tonight / until off. Ghosted = your crew flag renders without you and you contribute nothing to heat. Story posts always venue-anchored, never coordinate-anchored. Presence is off by default; planting a flag is always an explicit act.
keyFeatures.ceoQuestions: Intuitive: privacy you can explain in one sentence is part of passing the Snap Map 5-second bar. Friction: opt-in-by-act (plant flag) avoids the Instagram-Map backlash that kills trust before habit forms. Identity: 'aggregate-only heat, groups never individuals' is a stated Func constraint made into UI. Expansion: clean consent architecture is what lets venue-facing analytics ship later without scandal.

firstTimeUserStory: 0-10s: App opens ONTO the map — no feed, no tabs competing (Zenly rule). Velmont at night; three venues visibly burning with story rings of different thickness; one crew flag waving at Archive 9; a dashed ETA arc sliding toward The Vault. The scene is legible before any touch: bright ring = popping, flag = friends together, arc = someone's on the way. 10-25s: They tap the fattest ring. Camera pushes in, the Marquee rises, and a merged story reel from inside Archive 9 autoplays — crowd meter and £34 avg-spend beside it, two crew flags listed, a Rally button persistent at the bottom. They now hold the whole grammar: see heat → watch place → one tap to go. 25-45s: They pinch out past the city and hit the globe — Velmont glowing among lit cities — then pinch back in; the world-scale ambition lands wordlessly. 45-60s: A single soft prompt, the only onboarding copy in the experience: 'Plant your flag when you head out — your crew shows up together, never alone. Ghost anytime.' They close the app understanding the map, the privacy stance, and exactly what Friday is for. No tutorial screens anywhere.
differentiators: Heat generated BY the social graph: venue temperature is your extended network's check-ins and stories, so the utility compounds with the network — structurally uncopyable by venue-data utilities (Current, NOITE, LINES) and undone by none of the friend-map apps.

Group-first marks: crews fuse into flags and individuals never render alone — inverts Snap/Jagat's individual-avatar grammar, matches Func's thesis, and dissolves the person-tracking privacy objection by architecture rather than settings.
Map-only stories with 2h ember decay: no stories tab exists, so every content view is a discovery act, and brightness always means NOW — versus Instagram's stale 24h retrofit.
Rally: quorum-based group summoning with animated ETA arcs — plan and execution collapse onto one surface; competitors' OMW mechanics are individual-to-individual.

Trust on the map: vouch crests surface earned, attributable host standing at the join decision moment — no social map has reputation infrastructure, and it is the unlock for stranger-mixing (the pool) at night.

The Afterglow layer makes one surface serve both modes: peak-night live stage and off-day memory/status/anticipation — crew streaks and group home-bars extend Snap's individual Place Loyalty into Func's group grammar.
risks: Cold start / ghost-town map: ephemeral content makes sparsity visible and self-reinforcing. Mitigation is launch discipline — neighborhood-by-neighborhood, minimum-liveness gating per district, venue-posted stories and events/hours as non-UGC backfill so the map is never blank.

Content supply at night: people mid-night don't stop to post. Capture must be near-zero-friction (one-tap clip from the Marquee, RSVP'd events as prompted content moments) or rings stay thin and the core loop starves.

Privacy perception: even aggregate flags can be misread as tracking; one bad headline pre-habit is fatal (Instagram Map precedent). Ghost must be genuinely one tap, presence opt-in-by-act, and the 'never alone on the map' rule must hold with zero exceptions.

Vouch corruption: reciprocity inflation, vouch-farming rings, and a paid market if crests ever gate real access. Mitigations are designed in (scarcity, tenure, attribution, revocation, ring-discounting) but require ongoing enforcement, and v1 must keep a full non-vouch path.

Polish bar: the design's persuasion lives in animation craft (flag physics, ring decay, camera push). Zenly proved polish is the moat — which means under-resourced motion design makes this read as a gimmick.
Battery and background-location cost of presence detection; must copy Zenly's sleep-unless-watched engine or the app gets deleted for drain.
18+ UGC moderation: venue-anchored nightlife video needs review tooling and reporting from day one; a single incident story damages venue partnerships.
prototypeScope: Buildable now in the existing Expo/RN SVG prototype (/prototype, components/VelmontMap.tsx + WorldMap.tsx, data/velmont.ts): (1) Story Rings — replace flat venue dots with segmented SVG ring arcs (strokeDasharray on Circle) around the 8 existing venues; fake per-story timestamps in data/velmont.ts drive segment count and color (white→cyan→pink) with an Animated cooling loop; reuse the existing pulse Animated.Value. (2) Crew Flags — new CrewFlag component composing the existing AvatarStack on an SVG flagpole at 2-3 venues, driven by groups.ts membership + a mock 'out tonight' field; gentle wave via Animated skew. (3) Marquee — on venue tap, animate viewBox toward the venue (Animated interpolation of viewBox string or a scaled G transform) and raise a bottom sheet showing a crossfading static-image mock reel, crowd meter, existing costBreakdown totals (lib/cost.ts), flags present, and Rally button. (4) Rally — long-press handler → half-raised flag with greyed avatars, scripted accept sequence lighting avatars and raising the flag, plus dashed ETA arc Paths animating strokeDashoffset from district centroids to the venue. (5) Afterglow toggle chip — dims heat, draws a fading footprint Polyline across 3 venues from mock last-Friday data, shows a crew-streak flame badge and a 'home bar' crest on The Vault. (6) Ghost toggle in profile tab flipping the user out of their crew flag. Globe→city already exists via WorldMap. Explicitly out of prototype scope: real location/geofencing, real video, posting, vouch backend logic (crest is static mock with a tap-through 'Vouched by' card), widgets, and any moderation tooling — all faked with hand-authored data to sell the loop in a 3-minute demo."
